value.name: value
value.description:
The value of the currently active `Tab`. Use when the component is controlled.
When the value is `null`, no Tab will be active.

defaultValue.name: defaultValue
defaultValue.description:
The default value. Use when the component is not controlled.
When the value is `null`, no Tab will be active.

onValueChange.name: onValueChange
onValueChange.description:
Callback invoked when new value is being set.

The event `reason` is `'none'` for user-initiated changes, such as a click
or keyboard navigation; `'initial'` for the first automatic selection or
fallback in uncontrolled roots when `defaultValue` is omitted or
`undefined`, including when the implicit initial value is disabled or
missing; `'disabled'` for automatic fallback when the selected tab becomes
disabled in uncontrolled roots; or `'missing'` for automatic fallback when
the selected tab is removed, or when an explicit `defaultValue` never
matches a mounted tab in uncontrolled roots.

For automatic changes, the selected value can be `null` when no enabled Tab
is available as a fallback.

Automatic changes cannot be canceled; calling `eventDetails.cancel()` for
`'initial'`, `'disabled'`, or `'missing'` has no effect.

disabled.name: disabled
disabled.description:
Whether the Tab is disabled.

If a first Tab on a `<Tabs.List>` is disabled, it won't initially be selected.
Instead, the next enabled Tab will be selected.
However, it does not work like this during server-side rendering, as it is not known
during pre-rendering which Tabs are disabled.
To work around it, ensure that `defaultValue` or `value` on `<Tabs.Root>` is set to an enabled Tab's value.

Card.FullBleed.name: Card.FullBleed
Card.FullBleed.description:
A container that breaks out of the card's padding to span edge-to-edge.
Useful for full-width images, dividers, or embedded content.

Additional edge-bumping behavior based on placement:

- As the **first child** of `Card.Header`, it extends flush to the card's
  top edge — ideal for hero images.
- As the **only child** of `Card.Content`, it extends flush to the card's
  top edge when `Content` is the first card section, and to the bottom edge
  when it is the last.

Inter-sibling spacing inside `Card.Header` / `Card.Content` is consumer-
managed. To add space between a hero `FullBleed` and the following
siblings, compose the parent with `Stack` via the `render` prop:
`<Card.Header render={ <Stack direction="column" gap="lg" /> }>`. This
keeps `FullBleed` a direct child of `Card.Header` so the edge-bump still
fires, while `Stack` provides the gap.

Inside `CollapsibleCard`, place full-bleed media in `CollapsibleCard.Content`
(not the header). The trigger/panel gap is preserved by design.

Must be used as a direct child of `Card.Content` or `Card.Header`.

stories.name: With Visual
stories.snippet:
const WithVisual = () => <Stack gap="md" align="flex-start" justify="space-between">
    <Stack>
        <ControlledToggleControl
            help="Additional context that helps users understand what this setting does and when they might want to turn it on or off." />
    </Stack>
    <Stack
        align="center"
        justify="center"
        style={ {
            backgroundColor:
                'var(--wpds-color-background-surface-neutral-weak)',
            borderRadius: 'var(--wpds-border-radius-md)',
            flexShrink: 0,
            height: 'var(--wpds-dimension-size-lg)',
            width: 'var(--wpds-dimension-size-lg)',
        } }>
        <Icon icon={ wordpress } />
    </Stack>
</Stack>;
stories.description:
When adding a visual aid, prefer placing it at the trailing end of the row,
rather than placing it directly before the label, or moving the toggle to the trailing end.

dataviews-dataviewspicker.name: DataViewsPicker
dataviews-dataviewspicker.description:
`DataViewsPicker` renders a dataset allowing users to select one or multiple
items. It shares the layouts, search, and filtering of `DataViews` but is
geared toward choosing items rather than managing them.

reactComponentMeta.description:
`DataViewsPicker` renders a dataset allowing users to select one or multiple
items. It shares the layouts, search, and filtering of `DataViews` but is
geared toward choosing items rather than managing them.

view.name: view
view.description:
The current view configuration: layout type, filters, sorting,
pagination, search term, and visible fields.

onChangeView.name: onChangeView
onChangeView.description:
Callback invoked with the new view whenever the user changes it
(filtering, sorting, switching layout, changing page, etc.).
Consumers own the view state and must store the new value.

fields.name: fields
fields.description:
The fields describing each item's data: how to get and render a value,
plus its sorting and filtering capabilities.

actions.name: actions
actions.description:
The button actions that can be performed on items. Unlike `DataViews`,
pickers only support button actions (no modals).

search.name: search
search.description: Whether the global search input is displayed.

searchLabel.name: searchLabel
searchLabel.description: The accessible label and placeholder for the search input.

data.name: data
data.description:
The dataset to render, already filtered, sorted, and paginated
according to the current view.

isLoading.name: isLoading
isLoading.description: Whether the data is loading, in which case a loading state is shown.

paginationInfo.name: paginationInfo
paginationInfo.description: Pagination totals for the full dataset (not just the current page).

defaultLayouts.name: defaultLayouts
defaultLayouts.description:
The layouts the user can switch between, mapping each supported layout
type to view settings applied when switching to it (or `true` for
defaults). Only picker layouts (`pickerGrid`, `pickerTable`,
`pickerActivity`) are supported; other layout types are ignored.

selection.name: selection
selection.description:
The currently selected items, as a list of item ids. Selection is
always controlled in pickers, so this prop is required.

onChangeSelection.name: onChangeSelection
onChangeSelection.description:
Callback invoked with the new list of selected item ids whenever the
selection changes.

children.name: children
children.description:
Custom component tree rendered instead of the default layout
composition, using the internal `DataViewsPicker.*` sub-components.

config.name: config
config.description: Static configuration of the component's UI.

itemListLabel.name: itemListLabel
itemListLabel.description: The accessible label for the list of items rendered by the layout.

empty.name: empty
empty.description:
Content rendered when the dataset is empty (no items match the
current view).

onReset.name: onReset
onReset.description:
Callback to reset the view to its initial state, wired to the
"Reset view" button in the view options popover. When provided, the
view options toggle also shows a "modified" indicator. Pass `false` to
render the button disabled (the view is not modified); omit the prop
to hide the button altogether (no reset support).

getItemId.name: getItemId
getItemId.description:
Returns a unique id for an item. Required when items have no
string `id` property.

stories.name: Default
With Modal

accessibleWhenDisabled.name: accessibleWhenDisabled
accessibleWhenDisabled.description:
Whether to keep the button focusable when disabled.

In most cases, it is recommended to set this to `true`. Disabling a control without maintaining focusability
can cause accessibility issues, by hiding their presence from screen reader users,
or by preventing focus from returning to a trigger element.

Learn more about the [focusability of disabled controls](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/practices/keyboard-interface/#focusabilityofdisabledcontrols)
in the WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices Guide.

stories.name: Default
Primary
stories.description:
Primary buttons stand out with bold color fills, making them distinct
from the background. Since they naturally draw attention, each layout should contain
only one primary button to guide users toward the most important action.

stories.name: Secondary
stories.description: Secondary buttons complement primary buttons. Use them for standard actions that may appear alongside a primary action.

stories.name: Tertiary
stories.description: Tertiary buttons have minimal emphasis. Use them sparingly to subtly highlight an action.

stories.name: Link
stories.description:
Link buttons have low emphasis and blend into the page, making them suitable for supplementary actions,
especially those involving navigation away from the current view.

stories.name: Is Destructive
stories.description: Use this variant for irreversible actions. Apply sparingly and only for actions with significant impact.

components-modal.name: Modal

type.name: { describedby?: string | undefined; labelledby?: string | undefined; }

bodyOpenClassName.name: bodyOpenClassName
bodyOpenClassName.description:
Class name added to the body element when the modal is open.
If you use a custom class name, its styles must set `overflow: hidden`
to preserve the Modal's scroll lock.

children.name: children
children.description: The children elements.

className.name: className
className.description:
If this property is added, it will an additional class name to the modal
content `div`.

contentLabel.name: contentLabel
contentLabel.description:
If this property is added, it will be added to the modal content `div` as
`aria-label`.

Titles are required for accessibility reasons, see `aria.labelledby` and
`title` for other ways to provide a title.

focusOnMount.name: focusOnMount
focusOnMount.description:
Determines focus behavior when the modal opens.

- `"firstElement"` focuses the first tabbable element within.
- `"firstInputElement"` focuses the first value control within.
- `"firstContentElement"` focuses the first tabbable element within the modal’s content element.
- `true` focuses the element itself.
- `false` does nothing and _should not be used unless an accessible
   substitute behavior is implemented_.

headerActions.name: headerActions
headerActions.description:
Elements that are injected into the modal header to the left of the close button (if rendered).
Hidden if `__experimentalHideHeader` is `true`.

icon.name: icon
icon.description: If this property is added, an icon will be added before the title.

isDismissible.name: isDismissible
isDismissible.description:
If this property is set to false, the modal will not display a close icon
and cannot be dismissed.

isFullScreen.name: isFullScreen
isFullScreen.description: This property when set to `true` will render a full screen modal.

size.name: size
size.description:
If this property is added it will cause the modal to render at a preset
width, or expand to fill the screen. This prop will be ignored if
`isFullScreen` is set to `true`.

Note: `Modal`'s width can also be controlled by adjusting the width of the
modal's contents, or via CSS using the `style` prop.

onKeyDown.name: onKeyDown
onKeyDown.description: Handle the key down on the modal frame `div`.

onRequestClose.name: onRequestClose
onRequestClose.description: This function is called to indicate that the modal should be closed.

overlayClassName.name: overlayClassName
overlayClassName.description:
If this property is added, it will an additional class name to the modal
overlay `div`.

role.name: role
role.description:
If this property is added, it will override the default role of the
modal.

shouldCloseOnClickOutside.name: shouldCloseOnClickOutside
shouldCloseOnClickOutside.description:
If this property is added, it will determine whether the modal requests
to close when a mouse click occurs outside of the modal content.

shouldCloseOnEsc.name: shouldCloseOnEsc
shouldCloseOnEsc.description:
If this property is added, it will determine whether the modal requests
to close when the escape key is pressed.

style.name: style
style.description: If this property is added, it will be added to the modal frame `div`.

title.name: title
title.description:
This property is used as the modal header's title.

Titles are required for accessibility reasons, see `aria.labelledby` and
`contentLabel` for other ways to provide a title.

__experimentalHideHeader.name: __experimentalHideHeader
__experimentalHideHeader.description:
When set to `true`, the Modal's header (including the icon, title and
close button) will not be rendered.

_Warning_: This property is still experimental. “Experimental” means this
is an early implementation subject to drastic and breaking changes.

ref.name: ref
ref.description:
Allows getting a ref to the component instance.
Once the component unmounts, React will set `ref.current` to `null`
(or call the ref with `null` if you passed a callback ref).
